name: Moss Mat
desc: A macro study of moss and liverwort fighting for a slab of rock — compact acrocarpous cushions spread in every direction while thalloid liverwort runs in forking ribbons along its own axis, sporophyte setae rise from mature turf and nod their ripening capsules until they dehisce, and necrotic centres collapse back to bare stone for the spore rain to recolonise.

density.doc: how much of the turf is rendered as tufts + sporophytes, and how hard it rains spores

scale.doc: magnification — 0.35 is a wide slab of fine turf, 2.4 zooms to a few huge cushions

hue.doc: moss hue (liverwort always sits ~50 degrees off it)

moisture.doc: bias of the wet/dry cycle — dry turf is dull, brittle and slow, wet turf swells and saturates

style.doc: aesthetic — wet bright-field on damp granite; Prussian-blue photogram; sumi tonal wash on paper; clinical ironbow false-colour keyed to biomass

seed.doc: seeds the inoculation, the rock mottle and every colonisation decision

alpha.doc: opacity of the tufts and sporophytes over the mat
